headline: Republican Senator Bernie Moreno accused Anthropic's chief executive of an alarmist approach to AI in a letter sent as the company prepares to go public.
score_reason: Pool score kept: an official letter from a sitting senator, confirmed by his own press release; it is political criticism, not a policy change.
importance_line: It affects people who may be offered Anthropic shares, lawmakers weighing how to talk about AI risk, and Anthropic itself, but it is one senator's letter and it changes no policy.
summary: Axios reports, and the senator's release confirms, that Republican Senator Bernie Moreno of Ohio wrote to Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei on Monday 5 Oct, as the company prepares to go public, accusing him of an "alarmist approach" and saying he does not understand how Anthropic can ask Americans to invest while "warning those same Americans that your product could ultimately lead to their extinction". The letter answers Amodei's public warnings about AI, citing former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon, who quit saying Anthropic and OpenAI are "gambling with our lives", and follows the ABC News interview in our 30 Sep edition in which Amodei asked for stronger AI rules.
notes: Axios's own page returned a Cloudflare block (403). Facts read from Senator Moreno's own press release and full letter (moreno.senate.gov), The Next Web (says Axios first reported the letter) and Seeking Alpha via TradingView. Pool flags a follow-up of 1005:C05-03 (6abc Philadelphia, 4 Oct: Amodei calls for stronger regulation of AI, apparently the same ABC News exclusive printed as item 105 in our 30 Sep edition); the letter itself is new on 5 Oct. The letter says trading is expected as soon as October 2026, while Bloomberg (5 Oct edition item 5) reported a roadshow from 9 Nov and a listing in mid-November, so the entry gives no listing date.
